title: Canonical section-degree comparison respects tensor multiplication
statement: Let j:Z→X be a closed immersion, L invertible, j.ker²=0, n,e≥0, and D the canonical TensorBoundaryComparisonData j L n [lem-sc-square-zero-ideal-tensor-unit]. For f:O_Z→(j*L)^n and x:O_Z→((j*L)^n)^(e+1), transport their tensor product through the inverse pullback tensor comparison, pullback of tensorPowAddIso inverse, and the equality n+n(e+1)=n(e+2). The resulting section is the value at 1 of lambda inverse followed by f tensor x and D.a_(e+1) inverse. The first input section is tensorPowSection f 1 followed by D.a_0 inverse. This statement uses no graded algebra or presentation.

source.place: Tag 09MS, coherent-equation-ses and the direct-sum exact sequence following it; Tag 0B8S, cohomology-lemma-boundary-derivation-over-cup-product, the quotient action in the first paragraph of its proof.

proof.text: Substitute hD and expand boundarySectionDegreeIso into the recursive pullback-power comparison followed by tensorPowMulIso. Prove the inverse pullback-power addition equation by induction on its first exponent for an arbitrary lax monoidal functor. Its zero case uses the normalized monoidal unit; its successor uses tensorator associativity, associator naturality, and the inductive equation. Transport the monoidal structure along boundaryPullbackComparison; its tensorator is exactly boundaryPullbackTensorIso.inv.

Prove tensorPowAddIso associativity by induction and the monoidal pentagon. Induction on the number of blocks then proves tensorPowMulIso_add_inv. Apply this regrouping equation with block counts 1 and e+1. Expand tensorPowSection f 1 and tensorPowAddIso 1 (e+1): unitor and associator coherence cancel the unit factor. Naturality of eqToHom transports both the pullback and the block comparisons through hdeg; Nat.mul_add and Nat.one_add identify the resulting exponent casts.

Precompose the obtained morphism equality with the inverse left unitor of the unit module and evaluate at 1. Hom.comp_app, leftUnitor_inv_app, and tensorHom_app_tmulSection give exactly the two sections in the statement. Degree n=0 and e=0 require no separate nonvanishing hypothesis and are included by the two inductions.

lean.statement:
theorem tensorSectionProduct_comparison {X Z : Scheme.{u}} (j : Z ⟶ X)
    [IsClosedImmersion j] (L : X.Modules) [L.IsInvertible] (hI : j.ker ^ 2 = ⊥)
    (n : ℕ) (D : TensorBoundaryComparisonData j L n)
    (hD : canonicalTensorBoundaryComparisons j L hI n = D)
    (e : ℕ) (f : 𝟙_ Z.Modules ⟶ ((tensorPullback j).obj L).tensorPow n)
    (x : 𝟙_ Z.Modules ⟶ (((tensorPullback j).obj L).tensorPow n).tensorPow (e + 1))
    (hdeg : n * (0 + 1) + n * (e + 1) = n * ((e + 1) + 1)) :
    ((tensorPullback j).map (eqToHom (congrArg L.tensorPow hdeg))).app ⊤
      (((tensorPullback j).map
        (L.tensorPowAddIso (n * (0 + 1)) (n * (e + 1))).inv).app ⊤
        ((boundaryPullbackTensorIso j (L.tensorPow (n * (0 + 1)))
          (L.tensorPow (n * (e + 1)))).inv.app ⊤
          (tmulSection
            ((tensorPowSection f 1 ≫ (D.a 0).inv).app ⊤ (1 : Γ(Z, ⊤)))
            ((x ≫ (D.a e).inv).app ⊤ (1 : Γ(Z, ⊤)))))) =
      ((((λ_ (𝟙_ Z.Modules)).inv ≫ (f ⊗ₘ x)) ≫ (D.a (e + 1)).inv).app ⊤
        (1 : Γ(Z, ⊤)))
